subject: slime-only encounter
text: The slime achievement triggers on any encounter with only slimes, including a group of one Metal Slime.

evidence.quote: The achievement pops if the win an encounter with only slimes. So a group of 8 Metal Slimes will trigger it, and a group of 1 Metal Slime will also trigger it.

subject: item achievement
text: The item achievement checks inventory, so obtain the item with savestates, save, and reload in hardcore mode for it to pop.

evidence.quote: The achievement checks if the item is in your inv. So get it with savestates, save the game, and then reload the game in hardcore mode. The achievement should pop for hardcore mode.

subject: achievement set
text: The achievements were only tested on save File 1, so use File 1 to earn the correct achievements.

evidence.quote: Achievements have only been tested for File 1. Choose that to make sure you are earning the right achievements.

subject: Thy True Name
text: The name Loto is the answer for the Thy True Name achievement.

evidence.quote: "Loto" is Thy True Name

subject: name achievements
text: The name-based achievements only work in save slot 1.

evidence.quote: And they only work in Slot 1!

subject: Thou Shalt Not Be Selfish
text: Thou Shalt Not Be Selfish can be missed on the first ending dialogue, but beating the game again restores it.

evidence.quote: No missables, with the possible exception of "Thou shalt not be selfish!" That's an end game dialogue box, but if you miss it the first time, you can just beat the game again to get it.

subject: emulator core
text: Launching with the RetroArch FCEUmm core gave one player only half the achievements.

evidence.quote: Just launched the game with Retroarch FCEUmm core and got half the achievements... wtf just happened :(

subject: Metal Slime
text: The Metal Slime rare drop was very hard to obtain for one player.

evidence.quote: Mastered! This one is a lot harder than the first and the metal slime rare drop was pretty rough...

subject: Bullwong
text: Bullwong can drop the Wizard's Ring, but one player needed many grinding encounters before it dropped.

evidence.quote: Grinded Bullwongs from Level 22 to Level 39 before I got a Wizard's Ring to drop, and even at Level 40 it took me a couple of tries to beat Malroth.

subject: enemies that can wipe the party
text: Some enemies can wipe the party, but they only appear right after a save point, so little progress is lost.

evidence.quote: There exists some enemies in this game which can kill your whole party if you are unlucky, but these enemies can only be found right after a savepoint, so you will never lose more than a few minutes of progress if you meet these.

subject: exploration
text: Exploring naturally without a guide means little grinding is needed.

evidence.quote: If you explore the game naturally and don't use a guide, you will not need very much grinding.

subject: level 30 to 40
text: Grinding between level 30 and 40 is a grind for one player.

evidence.quote: Mastered! Not as hard as I remember but still a grind between lvls 30-40.

subject: lighthouse
text: The lighthouse has bad RNG and the final enemies are hard.

evidence.quote: Has super bad RNG in the lighthouse and of course those enemies at the end (Blizzard boys, i'm looking at you), but i'm happy with it.

subject: grinding time
text: One player spent 5-6 hours grinding to max level.

evidence.quote: Probably took 5-6 hours all told, don't want to think about getting to max level.

subject: last area
text: The last area has a major difficulty spike.

evidence.quote: Mastered! The difficulty spike in the last area was insane. Good set for a good game!

subject: last area enemies
text: Enemies in the last area hit very hard.

evidence.quote: Enemies really packed a punch, especially the ones in the last area.

subject: full playthrough
text: One player beat the game in 11.5 hours using speedup for grinding.

evidence.quote: Mastery #115! Took me 11.5 hours to beat with a small amount of help from a friend (and a lot of speedup for grinding).

subject: Cannock and Moonbrooke
text: Cannock and Moonbrooke get no useful offensive magic or MP until significantly leveled, so grinding is needed early.

evidence.quote: Problem is that Cannock and Moonbrooke are both spellcasters/mages and not well equipped for melee combat (Cannock becomes mid at melee at later levels). ... They don't get useful offensive magic and/or the MP to cast them until you level them up significantly, meaning that the game is unbalanced for 3/4 of your adventure roughly unless you go out of your way to grind.

subject: endgame
text: The main challenge is playing the whole game, and it gets rough toward the end.

evidence.quote: Pretty easy mastery for the most part, the main challenge here is just having to play through all of DQ2 for the NES, the game gets really rough towards the end.

subject: Rhone
text: A player reported a softlock near Rhone where no further enemies could be encountered.

evidence.quote: Got all the way to Rhone and ran into a softlock where I can't encounter any more enemies for some reason or another so goodbye DQ2 you are never being finished T_T

subject: dungeon exploration
text: Exploring dungeons yourself and avoiding running away makes the game less grindy.

evidence.quote: The game feels less grindy if you explore dungeons yourself and don't run away from fights much.

subject: Metal Slime
text: Metal Slimes give less experience than killing regular enemies.

evidence.quote: Metal Slimes are not even worth it in this game, killing regular enemies give you more exp.

subject: hero name uHkd or TUT
text: Naming the hero 'uHkd' or 'TUT' locks the RNG and removes encounters until you save.

evidence.quote: PROTIP: using 'uHkd' or 'TUT' as the hero's name locks the RNG and removes encounters until you save.

subject: Cloak of Wind
text: The name trick helps assemble the full party and reach the Cloak of Wind quickly, after which you return to Midenhall to grind.

evidence.quote: Useful to assemble your full party and get the Cloak of Wind very quickly. Then you can go back to Midenhall and start progressively grinding back.

subject: Wizard's Ring
text: Getting the Wizard's Ring to drop was very RNG-dependent for one player.

evidence.quote: Had some pretty awful RNG getting a Wizard Ring to drop, but all the grinding ended up making the final stretch relatively easy.

subject: Wizard's Ring
text: It took about 2 hours for a Bullwong to drop the Wizard's Ring.

evidence.quote: lo terrible es que me tomo 2 horas para que un bollwong me diera el anillo
evidence.translation: the terrible thing is it took me 2 hours for a bollwong to give me the ring

subject: achievement set
text: All achievements can be earned in one playthrough.

evidence.quote: Mastered! A wonderful set, you can get all the achievements in one playthrough.

subject: Ye Olde Evile Prieste
text: The Ye Olde Evile Prieste achievement is missable, since the game can be beaten without killing Hargon.

evidence.quote: Fun fact: "Ye Olde Evile Prieste" is actually a missable achievement. You can beat the game without killing Hargon.

subject: Hargon
text: Using the Chance spell on Hargon in battle may make him flee.

evidence.quote: If you use "Chance" spell in battle with him there is a chance that he flee from battle.

subject: monolith save point
text: After Hargon flees, the player must restart from the monolith save point.

evidence.quote: Happened to me, now need to go all over again from monolith save point :D

subject: key items
text: Certain key items could take hours to find using only in-game hints.

evidence.quote: It could've taken me hours to get certain key items with only the Ingame hints

subject: grinding
text: It really isn't that bad with speedup, according to this comment.

evidence.quote: Mastered! Finally... I abandoned it after my prior computer died and I lost the savefile, but it just occurred to me that it really isn't that bad with speedup.
